Popowo Koscielne Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Popowo n Bugiem, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Popowo Kościelne from 1781, when a diocesan inspector noted locals buried their dead in nearby Radzymin rather than a local cemetery - implying this cemetery came later. Its founding is confirmed by no later than the 1820s, based on a surviving tombstone for Jehuda, son of Aharon, who died in 1825. By 1921, 109 Jews lived in the village, and during WWII its Jews were deported to the Maków Mazowiecki Ghetto and later murdered. Unconfirmed reports suggest Germans used tombstones to build a field airport near Nasielsk; postwar sand extraction from the hillside created a steep slope that split the cemetery into upper and lower sections. Local priest Remigiusz Stacherski led cleanup efforts from 2009-2012.
